Description: At dawn, Edmund Galley locks Oswald into the pantry in the Kitchen at gunpoint and erupts into a fierce argument with the arriving John Hobbes, Annie Beaumont, and Tony Dauer. After briefly reaching a consensus to use the piano as an emergency gathering signal, everyone splits up to act separately.
Location: Kitchen (Kitchen)
Key Information:
  - Edmund Galley orders Oswald into the pantry inside the Kitchen, shuts the door, and locks it. Oswald is trapped inside and can only speak through the door.
  - The narrator adds: the pantry is considered part of the Kitchen (Kitchen), so it does not have an independent location code.
  - John Hobbes, Annie Beaumont, and Tony Dauer arrive at the Kitchen and confirm Oswald has been restrained in the pantry.
  - Annie Beaumont strongly demands that Edmund Galley release Oswald, believing he is the only one who knows the truth; Edmund Galley insists that "the situation is under control" and refuses to let him out.
  - Tony Dauer recognizes that the gun in Edmund Galley’s hand belongs to him, questions why it ended up with Edmund Galley, and demands its return.
  - Edmund Galley refuses to return Tony Dauer’s gun, saying he needs to keep control in his own house, and promises to return it when Tony Dauer leaves the villa.
  - Edmund Galley says he will only release Oswald if incidents keep happening, and claims they won’t happen again; Annie Beaumont explicitly rebuts his judgment.
  - John Hobbes proposes a unified emergency gathering signal: if anyone finds a new clue or needs to summon everyone, they should go to the Living room (Living room) and play the piano, and everyone should gather there.
  - Oswald asks whether he is included in the "gathering" rule; John Hobbes clearly states the summons does not include Oswald.
  - Edmund Galley demands that Annie Beaumont tell him Victoria Maseko’s location and says he wants to speak with her; Annie Beaumont refuses to cooperate.
  - After Edmund Galley leaves the Kitchen, Oswald continues talking with those remaining while trapped in the pantry, and tells John Hobbes he remembers attending Martha Galley’s wedding, suggesting they ask Martha Galley whom she married.
  - John Hobbes decides to go question Martha Galley and leaves the Kitchen; the others stay for now. The narrator notes the subsequent content will be split into the next file.
Characters:
  [Edmund Galley (Edmund Galley)] Person No. 6, the male owner of the villa.
    · Escorts Oswald into the pantry at gunpoint and locks him inside to control him.
    · Refuses to release Oswald immediately, insisting he can control the situation and claiming things will return to normal.
    · Says he wants to go find Victoria (No. 7) to talk.
    · Refuses to return Tony Dauer’s gun, arguing he needs to keep control in the villa.
    · Wants to talk to Eve Dauer and asks Annie Beaumont where she is; after being refused, he leaves the Kitchen on his own.
  [Oswald (Oswald)] Person No. 3, forcibly restrained by Edmund Galley and locked into the pantry.
    · Is forced into the pantry and locked in, showing fear and begging not to be killed.
    · While trapped, can still hear the outside conversation and responds through the door.
    · After Edmund Galley leaves, gives John Hobbes a new memory clue: he attended Martha Galley’s wedding and suggests asking Martha Galley whom she married.
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, an outsider who mediates and tries to establish communication rules.
    · Upon arriving at the Kitchen, confirms Oswald has been locked in the pantry.
    · Proposes using piano playing in the Living room as a unified signal to summon everyone.
    · Explicitly states the gathering rule does not include Oswald.
    · After receiving Oswald’s clue about Martha Galley’s wedding, decides to go question Martha Galley.
  [Annie Beaumont (Annie Beaumont)] Person No. 2, strongly opposed to Edmund Galley’s controlling behavior.
    · Demands that Edmund Galley release Oswald immediately, believing he holds key truths.
    · Rebuts Edmund Galley’s assessment of the situation, believing he completely misunderstands the danger.
    · Refuses to disclose Eve Dauer’s location; the confrontation is clear.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony Dauer)] Person No. 4, recognizes the gun and demands it be returned.
    · Points out that the gun Edmund Galley is holding belongs to him and demands its immediate return.
    · States clearly he will not leave the villa until the truth is established.
    · Feels confused and angry about the lack of transparency among the group.
